title: Tensor products of irreducible algebras over a separably closed field
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed]. Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative unital $k$-algebras, meaning commutative unital rings with fixed unital homomorphisms from $k$. Suppose $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] are irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Equip $A\otimes_kB$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a\prime\otimes b\prime)=aa\prime\otimes bb\prime$ and unit $1\otimes1$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kB)$ is irreducible. Irreducibility includes nonemptiness. No finite-generation, reducedness, or field hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Tag 00I7, lemma-separably-closed-irreducible: unique-minimal-prime formulation, equivalently irreducibility of the nonempty spectra.

proof.text: Choose the algebraic closure Ω of k by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-pc-kbar-pure-insep], Ω/k is purely inseparable, in every characteristic. Set AΩ = Ω ⊗[k] A, BΩ = Ω ⊗[k] B, R = AΩ/nilradical(AΩ), and S = BΩ/nilradical(BΩ).

For each k-algebra C = A, B, A ⊗[k] B, apply the affine Mathlib theorem PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap_of_isPurelyInseparable k Ω C. Composing with tensor commutation identifies Spec(Ω ⊗[k] C) with Spec C. Homeomorph.irreducibleSpace_iff transports irreducibility. This uses the affine theorem directly, with no scheme fibre-product construction.

source.place: Tag 00I7, first paragraph, using the affine homeomorphism of Tag 0BRA.

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime] to AΩ and BΩ. Their nilradicals are prime, so the quotient-domain instance gives IsDomain R and IsDomain S, including nontriviality.

For any ring C and ideal I ≤ nilradical C, the quotient map is surjective and its kernel is I. Thus [lem-pur-all-element-powers-spectrum-homeomorphism], with exponent 1 for every target element, gives a homeomorphism Spec C ≃ Spec(C/I). For any two k-algebras D,E, let I be the extension of nilradical E along includeRight : E → D ⊗[k] E. Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap and preservation of nilpotence under ring maps give I ≤ nilradical(D ⊗[k] E). Algebra.TensorProduct.tensorQuotientEquiv identifies its quotient with D ⊗[k] (E/nilradical E). Consequently reducing the right factor preserves the tensor spectrum; commute to reduce the left factor as well. This sequential quotient construction avoids constructing a combined quotient kernel.

source.place: Tag 00I7, second paragraph; elementary tensor-quotient presentation.

proof.text: Use Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange and Algebra.TensorProduct.assoc to identify AΩ ⊗[Ω] BΩ with Ω ⊗[k] (A ⊗[k] B). Compose the ring-equivalence spectrum homeomorphism, the purely inseparable homeomorphism of Step 2 and the two reduction homeomorphisms of Step 4. This gives Spec(A ⊗[k] B) ≃ Spec(R ⊗[Ω] S).

source.place: Tag 00I7, first displayed base-change identification and second-paragraph reduction.

proof.text: The nonzero Ω-vector spaces R,S have nonzero tensor product U by [lem-pur-field-vector-space-tensor-nontrivial]. If x,y are nonzero elements of U with xy=0, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-type-limit] supplies finite-type Ω-subalgebras R′, S′ and nonzero x′,y′ in R′ ⊗[Ω] S′ with x′y′=0. The subalgebras inherit domain structures from R,S. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algclosed-finite-type-tensor-domain] to R′,S′ to contradict that product. Thus U has no zero divisors and is nontrivial, hence is a domain.

source.place: Tag 00I7, second and final paragraphs, using Tag 00I3(2).

proof.text: A domain has prime zero ideal and irreducible prime spectrum, by the domain instance of [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime]. Transport the irreducibility of Spec U through the homeomorphism of Step 5. The underlying space of Spec(CommRingCat.of C) is definitionally PrimeSpectrum C, so this proves the stated scheme-spectrum conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00I7, lemma-separably-closed-irreducible; M9 Lean proof follows the purely inseparable scalar extension, reduction of factors, and finite-type zero-divisor reduction. Mathlib affine spectrum homeomorphisms replace scheme fibre products, and successive tensor-quotient equivalences replace the combined nil-kernel calculation. Private proved helper patterns are adapted from WeilConjectures.FieldTheory.SepClosedTensorReduction.
